description:
Programme Overview

The Erasmus Mundus Master's Programme in Human Rights Policy and Practice (EMHRPP) is a , fully funded two-year joint master's degree offered by a consortium of four European universities. This program is designed for students who aspire to become future leaders in human rights policy, practice, and research, providing a multidisciplinary and international learning experience across multiple countries.

Key Objectives

  • Develop advanced expertise in human rights theory, policy, and practice
  • Foster international understanding through cross-cultural education
  • Build professional networks across Europe and beyond
  • Prepare graduates for leadership roles in human rights organizations, governments, and civil society

Participating Universities

UniversityLocationSpecialization
University of GothenburgSwedenHuman rights theory, research methods
University of DeustoSpainHuman rights in policy and practice, business and human rights
University of RoehamptonEngland, UKHuman rights and humanitarianism, transitional justice
University of OsloNorwayInternational human rights law, institutions

Students typically study at two or more of these universities during the program, experiencing different academic environments and cultural contexts.

Funding Details & Benefits

  • Monthly stipend: €1,000 per month for 24 months
  • Tuition fees: Full coverage for entire program
  • Travel & installation: Contribution towards travel and installation costs (paid in two installments)
  • Health insurance: Comprehensive coverage for full two years
  • Research costs: Funding for thesis research and fieldwork as needed
  • Joint degree from all four consortium universities
  • Access to extensive research networks and resources
  • Join a global network of human rights professionals

Eligibility Criteria

  • Academic background: Hold a bachelor's degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field such as law, social sciences, humanities, or international relations
  • Academic excellence: Demonstrate strong academic performance (typically minimum GPA of 3.0/4.0 or equivalent)
  • Human rights experience: Have relevant experience in human rights practice, research, or advocacy (professional or volunteer)
  • English proficiency: IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL 90 (specific requirements may vary)
  • Nationality: Be a citizen of a country other than the European Union (for the scholarship category; EU students can apply for self-funded positions)

Preferred Qualifications

  • Professional experience in human rights organizations, NGOs, or related fields
  • Research experience with research methods and academic writing
  • Additional language skills relevant to human rights work
  • Multicultural experience in international environments

Application Process

  1. Prepare application documents
  2. Submit online application
  3. Pay application fee (if applicable)
  4. Wait for selection results
  5. Accept scholarship and prepare for enrollment

Required Documents

  • Application form (completed online)
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Letter of motivation
  • Academic transcripts
  • Proof of degree
  • English proficiency proof (TOEFL/IELTS)
  • Letters of recommendation (typically two academic references)
  • Human rights experience documentation
  • Passport copy
  • Photograph

Timeline & Deadlines

MilestoneDate
Application opensAutumn 2026 (expected September/October)
Application deadline8 January 2027 (for scholarship consideration)
Review periodJanuary-February 2027
InterviewsFebruary-March 2027
NotificationMarch-April 2027
Program startSeptember 2027

Official Application Portal

https://www.emhrpp.com/

Official Links

  • Program Website: https://www.emhrpp.com
  • University of Gothenburg: https://www.gu.se/en/study-gothenburg/human-rights-in-policy-and-practice-mr1111
  • Erasmus+ Programme: https://erasmus-plus.ec.europa.eu/

Important Notes

  • No age limit for the EMHRPP scholarship.
  • Students typically study at multiple universities in the consortium.
  • Graduates join a global network of EMHRPP alumni working in human rights organizations, governments, international bodies, and academia.
